primaryQuery: WPA2 or WPA3 for smart home devices
readerQuestion: Should I use WPA3-only, WPA2/WPA3 transitional mode, or a separate WPA2 network so older smart-home devices keep working without weakening the rest of my home?
selectedBecause: Reddit and Home Assistant Community discussions repeatedly ask whether WPA3 works reliably with smart plugs, sensors, speakers, Matter devices, and ESPHome hardware, while current Google results split the answer between generic protocol comparisons, router-vendor advice, and isolated troubleshooting threads. Google and Apple both warn that older WPA2 clients can fail even in transitional mode; current ESPHome documentation and its merged implementation work confirm that authentication support still depends on the device platform. The supplied Search Console export, opportunity CSV, keyword map, and ownership strategy were reviewed first and contain no WPA2/WPA3 query or assigned owner path. This question beats the other candidates because it has one clear homeowner decision, applies across brands and ecosystems, stays useful as households mix old and new devices, fits Tara's reliable local-home guidance, exposes a real result gap around safe fallback networks and local discovery, and does not duplicate an existing Tara article.

demandSignals.evidence: A direct question asks whether WPA3 works consistently on a smart-device network; replies report mixed outcomes across Kasa plug models and firmware, a Zemismart Matter bulb, and a Sonoff plug running ESPHome.
A homeowner with older Kasa switches asks how to keep WPA2-only devices after moving the main network to WPA3, illustrating concrete migration and fallback-network intent.

A Home Assistant Community setup question asks which Wi-Fi authentication mode is best for Home Assistant and home automation after WPA3 connection trouble, and explicitly notes the lack of a direct answer.

An ESPHome troubleshooting discussion isolates WPA2/WPA3 transitional mode as the practical difference from reliable WPA2-only connection behavior, showing that mixed mode can still fail in real homes.

A merged ESPHome change added explicit minimum WPA, WPA2, and WPA3 authentication handling with secure defaults and platform limits, confirming that client-stack support remains a live compatibility concern.

The exact-query review is led by a router-vendor comparison and community reports; it lacks one vendor-neutral homeowner guide that handles WPA3-only, transitional mode failures, a WPA2-AES fallback, and local smart-home communication together.

searchReview.query: WPA2 or WPA3 for smart home devices
searchReview.intent: The reader wants one safe router-security setting that protects newer devices, keeps required older smart devices online, and gives them a practical fallback when WPA3 or transitional mode breaks setup.
searchReview.resultGap: Current results explain that WPA3 is stronger and transitional mode permits WPA2, but they rarely warn that some legacy devices fail merely when WPA3 is advertised. They also fail to distinguish WPA2/WPA3 transitional mode from the obsolete WPA/WPA2 or TKIP choices, separate authentication from the 2.4 GHz band, and explain why an isolated guest network may break Matter or local control. A clear test, rollback, and constrained WPA2-AES fallback plan is missing.

officialSources.name: Apple recommended Wi-Fi router settings
officialSources.supports: WPA3 Personal is preferred, WPA2/WPA3 Transitional supports older devices, WPA2 Personal with AES is the fallback, and WEP, WPA, TKIP, and open security should be avoided.

officialSources.name: Google Nest Wi-Fi band and WPA3 guidance
officialSources.supports: Legacy WPA2 devices can experience connection problems while WPA3 transitional mode is enabled, and changing the WPA3 setting restarts the network.

officialSources.name: Google Nest Wifi Pro product guidance
officialSources.supports: Nest Wifi Pro is managed through Google Home, is Matter-enabled, and includes a Thread border router, supporting the guide's concrete router example.

officialSources.name: ESPHome Wi-Fi component documentation
officialSources.supports: Current ESPHome exposes WPA, WPA2, and WPA3 minimum authentication modes, recommends WPA2 or newer, warns against WPA and TKIP, and limits WPA3-only configuration to ESP32.

officialSources.name: NSA best practices for securing a home network
officialSources.supports: Home networks should use WPA3 or WPA2/WPA3 when older-device compatibility requires it, use a long passphrase, update routers, and segment less-trusted IoT devices.

officialSources.name: Connectivity Standards Alliance Matter network guidance
officialSources.supports: Guest-network client isolation can block Matter setup and local controller communication, so a legacy-device fallback must preserve the local communication required by the household's platform.

officialSources.name: TP-Link WPA2 and WPA3 comparison
officialSources.supports: WPA3 strengthens password protection, mixed mode supports newer and older clients, and some very old devices can still require WPA2-only mode.

officialSources.name: TP-Link Tapo P110M product page
officialSources.supports: The current US model page lists 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, Matter and Apple Home paths, local app access during an internet outage, and remote app control without stating a WPA mode.

officialSources.name: TP-Link Kasa EP25 product and HomeKit setup guidance
officialSources.supports: TP-Link's current HomeKit troubleshooting applies to EP25 and tells users to change WPA3-only to Auto or WPA2/WPA3 when Apple Home setup times out.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant TP-Link Smart Home integration
officialSources.supports: Home Assistant lists Tapo P110M and Kasa EP25 support, connects locally for data and control, documents newer-device credential requirements, and warns about discovery across subnets.

existingCoverage.decision: No Tara article owns Wi-Fi authentication compatibility. The mesh guide owns bands, SSIDs, coverage, and roaming; the router-change guide only notes preserving a compatible security mode; the VLAN guide owns segmentation architecture; the security-basics guide is broad hygiene; and the commercial hub page retains local-hub buying intent. This new URL will own the specific WPA3-only versus transitional versus WPA2-AES decision, the safe compatibility test, and the local-control caveat without retargeting any existing owner query.
